shot.prose: The page is a documentation landing page for a no-build, native-ESM web framework, and the H1 states that purpose immediately and unmistakably — hierarchy is strong from the first glance, with the oversized bold heading followed by stat cards that act as a visual proof-point. The two-column layout (white sidebar left, light-gray content right) is conventional and legible, and the sidebar's section labels CORE and STYLES provide a clear structural map, though their uppercase gray weight is thin enough to be almost invisible as wayfinding. The single most noticeable spatial problem is that the main content column terminates around 70% of the viewport width — the code block's right edge sits roughly at x=890 out of 1280 — leaving the rightmost third of the screen as a large featureless gray zone that neither serves readability nor feels intentional. None of the sidebar navigation items carry any active or selected state, so a reader cannot orient themselves to where they currently are in the site; "Start here" looks identical to "Sidebar" and every other item. The five stat cards in a row are visibly unequal in width: the first two ("714" and "21 KB") are noticeably wider than the three narrower "0" cards beside them, making the row feel lopsided rather than uniform. The H1 starts close to the top edge of the content pane with minimal padding above it, giving the impression the page begins mid-breath. Contrast is good throughout — dark text on gray reads cleanly, the `import` pill and `/path/page.js` inline codes are legible, and the dark code block is well-framed with no floating surfaces. Alignment along the left margin is consistent: heading, body text, stat cards, and code block all share the same left edge. At the bottom of the sidebar a gray circle sits unlabelled beside the gear icon — its function (avatar? theme toggle?) is opaque with no label or recognisable icon. The page is largely typographic with the stat-card numbers as the only graphic emphasis; the sidebar icons are decorative at their size.

shot.prose: This is a daily AI task dashboard — "Today, ranked →" announces the purpose plainly and the four running cards immediately below it fulfil that promise, so the page's intent is clear at a glance. **Layout** is legible: the sidebar-plus-content split works, and the card stack reads naturally top-to-bottom with no stray elements sitting out of place. **Spacing** has a hitch: the gap between the "Today, ranked →" subtitle and the "ACTIVE 4" section label is visibly looser than the gap between that label and the first card, producing an uneven rhythm in the upper content zone. **Hierarchy** functions well — the bold date dominates, orange task names pull the eye next, and right-aligned model names (opus-5, fable-5) sit quietly as metadata without competing. **Contrast** is the sharpest concern: the word "dispatched" below the progress description in the first (vision-fixes) card is so faint on white that it nearly disappears, and the gray narrative lines in the mastermind-shots and vision-sweep cards ("Cycle 3 — vision-after…", "dry-run: 19 pages…") demand deliberate focus to read. **Alignment** is tidy — card left edges, progress bar rails, and right-anchored labels all share consistent horizontal positions. The right side of every card carries only a thin sliver of margin before the viewport boundary, making the content feel squeezed against that edge. Above "2026-08-17" there is roughly 60 px of empty white that contributes nothing, leaving the top of the content area feeling slack compared to the densely packed cards below. Cards read clearly as white surfaces against the light-gray page, so no missing-background problem exists. The small gray circle at the bottom-right of the sidebar is a dead spot: no icon, no label, no hover state visible — it reads as an abandoned placeholder rather than a reachable control. There is no obvious route to tasks beyond these four, so the overview feels complete only if the user already knows "ACTIVE 4" is the full picture.

shot.prose: The page announces its purpose confidently — "DesignTool," a code-import snippet, and one clear prose paragraph establish what this is within a single glance, so purpose lands. Layout is a straightforward two-column: the left sidebar carries the navigation tree and the main area holds the tab bar, code block, and prose, all legibly arranged. However, the main body content column occupies only roughly the left two-thirds of the available main-area width, leaving an unbroken empty gray band on the right that spans nearly a third of the content area — this dead zone feels like a missing right column rather than deliberate breathing room, especially because the full-width tab header above it has no such gap. The vertical gap between the tab bar and the top edge of the dark code block is very compressed, giving the first piece of content almost no space to breathe before it begins. Hierarchy is somewhat undermined mid-page by the bold ⚠ paragraph, which commands strong visual weight before the reader has even finished the introductory sentences — the warning is relevant but the bold + symbol combination promotes it above the code sample that arguably should rank first. Contrast is solid throughout: the dark code block with orange keywords is crisp, and the dark-chip inline code tags (`width-used`, `repetition`, `heading-offset`) in the dense prose are legible against the light body. Alignment is clean — the left edge of the code block and the prose below it share the same indent, and the tab labels are evenly spaced across the header. The four cards at the very bottom of the visible area (Layout library, Taste, Test corpus, Site audit) are cut off by the viewport with no gradient, shadow, or arrow cue to signal that scrolling reveals more — a reader whose eye reaches the bottom of the prose may not recognize them as interactive entry points. A small circular element sits unlabelled at the lower-right corner of the sidebar; it carries no icon that signals its function, leaving it opaque. The page is almost entirely typographic; the code block is the single non-text element above the fold and it earns its place.

shot.prose: The page is a live AI-task monitor: a left sidebar for navigation and a content column showing active job cards grouped by timestamp. That purpose becomes clear only once the eye reaches the "ACTIVE 4" label and the first card — the oversized "AI" heading above gives no hint of what the content is or why you'd be here. Between the "AI" h1 and the "ACTIVE 4" section there is a vertical gap nearly as tall as two full card rows, creating a sluggish start that makes the page feel like it loads late; the top-right quadrant of the content area — roughly the right half of that same zone — is entirely empty gray, which compounds the imbalance and wastes real estate that could carry a subtitle, a live count, or at minimum nothing more conspicuous than it currently is. The "6:34 PM" and "4:40 PM" timestamps that divide the card groups are styled the same as secondary metadata — small, muted gray — so they fail to register as structural dividers; the eye skips them and the grouping logic is invisible at a glance. Contrast in the description lines ("dispatched", "dry-run: 19 pages × 3 widths…") is on the low side against the near-white card surface but probably passable. Card alignment is clean and consistent across both left edges and progress-bar baselines; nothing appears clipped against the viewport edges. The multi-colour progress bar segments (orange, green, gray in varying proportions) carry no legend, so the segments' meaning — stages? agent types? completion vs. queued? — is opaque to a new viewer. Sidebar icons and labels are well-paired and alignment is orderly throughout.

shot.prose: The page is a living component catalog for a UI framework, and the intro text ("Every card is a live call…") communicates that purpose clearly in the first three lines — good. The two-column structure (filter sidebar left, component grid right) is legible and the orange **EVERYTHING 19** pill leaves no doubt which filter is active, giving hierarchy a solid anchor alongside the oversized "UI" heading. Spacing inside the filter sidebar is consistent — the category rows (SURFACES 5, DATA 5…) carry equal rhythm — but there is a conspicuously large vertical gap between the bottom of the intro paragraph ("…below it.") and the search box / SURFACES heading below it, effectively splitting the page into a header region and a content region with dead air between them. The "Filter modules…" placeholder text inside the middle SURFACES card is a very pale gray against a white input field; it is near-invisible and almost certainly fails contrast requirements. Contrast elsewhere is solid: body text, component labels, and the orange accents all read cleanly. The "Delete branch?" dialog card on the far right of the SURFACES row presses close to the content column's right edge, with noticeably less padding than the left card enjoys on its left side, producing a lopsided feel in that row. Alignment across the component name row (Card, Toolbar, Panel) is consistent, and the sidebar nav edges are flush and orderly. The live component previews — stat tiles, accordion questions, progress bars, timeline entries — earn every pixel; there is no gratuitous decoration, and the page is almost entirely functional content. The sidebar navigation links (Start here, AI, FAQ…) are mid-gray on a light-gray background; they are legible but noticeably lower in contrast than what the orange active states imply the design is capable of.

shot.prose:
This is a documentation page for a framework's "Core" section, and its purpose lands immediately — the "Core" heading, the opening code block, and the grid of seven named cards together communicate "here is what this module is and what belongs to it" without requiring any scrolling. Hierarchy is strong: the large bold `Core` h1 dominates, the two explanatory paragraphs follow naturally in weight, and the card grid reads as a secondary catalogue layer. Contrast is good throughout — the dark code block with coloured syntax is legible, the inline code badges (dark field, light text) sit cleanly against the paragraph background, and the orange underline on "Item's own record" stands out as a deliberate link without overwhelming the sentence. Alignment in the sidebar is tidy and consistent; icon and label pairs line up evenly, and the CORE / STYLES section labels provide a secondary rhythm without competing with the nav items.

The one hard edge problem is the rightmost card in the first card row — **App** — whose right border sits flush against, or possibly just beyond, the right edge of the content container, with no visible trailing gap; every other card has space on both sides, so this asymmetry reads as a clipping error rather than intent. The vertical gap between the last body paragraph ("…core rather than an opt-in.") and the top of the card grid is noticeably tighter than the gap between the `Core` heading and the code block above it, making the transition feel rushed. The unlabelled grey circle sitting in the bottom-right corner of the sidebar carries no icon and no tooltip visible in this frame, leaving its purpose completely opaque — it is the only control on screen that cannot be identified at a glance. Finally, the space between the `Core` h1 and the code block directly below it is quite compressed; the heading and the dark code surface nearly touch, which flattens the visual breath that the rest of the page enjoys between its sections.
